I collaborated closely with product managers, designers, backend engineers, and QA throughout the development lifecycle, from requirements and implementation to testing and production delivery.

I also incorporated GitHub Copilot into my workflow for code exploration, implementation planning, refactoring, and AI-assisted development.
items.overview:
NewHomeSource is a large-scale real estate platform that helps homebuyers discover new construction homes, communities, and builders across the United States.

I contributed to the evolution of the platform by developing and improving customer-facing experiences, integrating frontend features with backend services, and supporting a scalable and maintainable frontend architecture.

items.headline: Interwell health - Serving patients
items.tech_stack:
- Next.js
- React
- TypeScript
- Sitecore XM Cloud
- Sitecore JSS
- Storybook
- Tailwind CSS
- shadcn/ui
- Vercel
- Figma
- Vercel
- Radix
items.my_role:
As a Full-Stack Developer, I helped define and implement the frontend architecture around Next.js and the emerging Sitecore XM Cloud platform.

I worked closely with a dedicated Sitecore advocate to understand the new platform and adapted a custom Next.js boilerplate to work with XM Cloud. I also developed custom integrations and plugins to support Sitecore-specific requirements, including error page handling and content-driven page rendering.

To keep frontend development moving independently from the backend, I introduced Storybook and built reusable UI components that could later be connected to Sitecore "components".
items.key_points:
Helped establish the frontend architecture for one of our team's early Sitecore XM Cloud implementations, working through evolving documentation and platform requirements.

Adapted a custom Next.js architecture and developed plugins and integrations to ensure the application worked correctly with Sitecore XM Cloud, including custom error page handling.

Introduced Storybook to enable component-driven development, allowing the frontend team (me) to build and test UI components independently while the backend team worked on Sitecore schemas and content structures.

Built reusable UI components and responsive experiences using Tailwind CSS and Radix/ui, accelerating development while maintaining consistency across pages and layouts.
items.overview:
Redesign and development of the Interwell Health website using Next.js and Sitecore XM Cloud, with a strong focus on modern UI, animations, reusable components, and a flexible content-driven architecture.

The project was built during the early adoption of XM Cloud, when the platform and its documentation were still evolving, making the integration a significant technical challenge.

items.my_role:
As Co-Founder and Developer, I was responsible for translating the visual identity created by Bruno into a responsive and interactive web experience.

I implemented the frontend, animations, deployment, and domain configuration, including a dedicated subdomain for the studio's interactive brand style guide.

[ui.lustudio](https://lustudio.netlify.app/)
items.key_points:
Co-founded the studio and built its digital presence from the ground up, transforming the brand's visual direction into a complete web experience.

Developed responsive interfaces and custom animations, including the animated hero experience that introduces the brand when users first enter the website.

Configured the production deployment and custom domain infrastructure, including a dedicated subdomain for the studio's branding and UI style guide.

The project also gave me hands-on experience beyond development, including defining a digital service offering and exploring how to turn design and engineering skills into a small business.
items.overview:
LU Studio is an independent digital studio founded by my brother, Bruno Gatjens, and me with the goal of helping small and medium-sized businesses build a strong digital presence through high-quality design and development at accessible prices.

Bruno led the visual design and branding, while I focused on bringing the experience to life through frontend development, animations, responsive implementation, and the technical architecture of the website.

items.my_role:
As a Full-Stack Developer, I worked across the React/Ionic frontend, Node.js serverless APIs, and PostgreSQL database hosted on AWS.

I designed and implemented the Contentful content model used to manage shows, activities, assets, and event-specific content. I also built internal admin tools for generating user and order reports and creating QR codes for individual event activities.
items.key_points:
Built features end-to-end across the customer-facing application, serverless backend, database, CMS, and internal administration tools.

Designed the Contentful headless CMS schema to support multiple shows and event-specific content without requiring application deployments.

Developed an admin dashboard for operational workflows, including user and order reporting and QR code generation for event activities.

Integrated Prisma with PostgreSQL and deployed the database infrastructure on AWS to support users, orders, authentication, authorization, and event interactions.
items.overview:
An interactive event platform built for Elanco customers to discover products, participate in activities, win prizes, and engage with the brand during live events and shows.

The platform was designed to support multiple Elanco events, combining a mobile-first customer experience with a flexible content management system and internal administration tools.

items.my_role:
As a Frontend Developer, I worked closely with the design team to translate the visual direction into reusable React components and interactive web experiences.

I implemented custom CSS and JavaScript animations, integrated Gatsby for content management, and helped establish frontend patterns that made components easier to reuse across different sections and projects.
items.key_points:
Collaborated with the design team to create a small design system covering reusable components, typography, icons, branding, layouts, and frontend best practices.

Developed reusable React components and custom CSS/JavaScript animations designed to work across multiple sections and digital experiences.

Focused on creating a consistent relationship between design and development, establishing reusable patterns rather than implementing each page independently.
items.overview:
Hangar Worldwide’s website was built as a modern, content-driven experience using React and Gatsby, with a strong focus on visual design, animations, and reusable frontend components.

The project was developed in close collaboration with the design team, creating a flexible foundation that could be reused and extended across different pages and future digital experiences.

items.headline: NI - Solutions from Emerson
items.tech_stack:

- SCSS

- Lighthouse

items.my_role:
As a Frontend Developer, I helped design the Angular architecture used to build small applications that could run and communicate within the AEM platform.

Over approximately six months, I developed multiple mini-apps, reusable UI components, and integrations while progressively redesigning key areas of NI.com.

I also worked on measuring and improving frontend performance, using tools such as Lighthouse and Core Web Vitals to identify rendering, loading, and layout stability issues.
items.key_points:
Helped define an Angular architecture for independent mini-applications that could integrate with Adobe Experience Manager while allowing the platform to be modernized incrementally.

Built a large collection of reusable components and integrations used to progressively redesign a website with thousands of existing pages.

Measured and optimized frontend performance using Lighthouse and Core Web Vitals, focusing on areas such as LCP, CLS, asset loading, rendering performance, and overall page experience.

Worked closely with design and backend teams to ensure new components were performant, reusable, and compatible with the existing AEM infrastructure.
items.overview:
Large-scale redesign of NI.com, an enterprise website with thousands of pages powered by Adobe Experience Manager (AEM).

The project followed a progressive redesign strategy, modernizing the platform in stages while building reusable components and multiple Angular mini-applications integrated with the existing AEM ecosystem.

I also created a custom Gatsby theme, configured deployment pipelines and domains, and supported two developers as they learned React and Gatsby while contributing to the project.
items.key_points:
Designed the Gatsby architecture and built a reusable component foundation to support consistent development across the website.

Created a custom Gatsby theme to reuse common components, layouts, styles, and frontend patterns across multiple web projects.

Translated Figma designs into responsive interfaces and implemented custom animations to create a more polished and interactive user experience.

Configured domains and deployment pipelines, supporting the project from development through production delivery.

Mentored two developers while working on the project, helping them learn React and Gatsby and supporting them as they started contributing to production websites.

As a Full-Stack Developer, I worked across the React Native mobile application, React web application, and Node.js backend services.

I developed application features, integrated the frontend applications with shared APIs, managed application state with Redux, and contributed to the AWS-based infrastructure and MySQL data layer supporting the platform.
items.key_points:
Developed features for a cross-platform ecosystem that included a React Native mobile application and a React web application sharing the same Node.js backend services.

Implemented API integrations and Redux-based state management to support real-time case management workflows and communication across the platform.

Contributed to backend services and MySQL data integrations while working with AWS infrastructure supporting the applications.

Worked across mobile, web, backend, and cloud components, gaining end-to-end experience building and integrating a production application across multiple platforms.
items.overview:
OR Tracker is a cloud-based application designed to provide medical center teams and patients with a centralized communication hub and access to real-time case management information.

The platform included both a React Native mobile application and a React web application, connected to a shared Node.js backend and cloud infrastructure hosted on AWS.

items.headline: ArmorAll Redesign
items.tech_stack:
- Drupal
- Jekyll
- JavaScript
- SCSS
- HTML
- Gulp
- Responsive Web Design
- Frontend Animations
items.my_role:
As a Frontend Lead, I helped establish an approach that separated frontend development from the Drupal implementation, allowing frontend and backend teams to work in parallel.

I built the initial website using Jekyll, creating reusable templates, responsive styles, and interactive functionality that could later be integrated into Drupal and connected to CMS-managed content.
items.key_points:
Helped establish a development workflow that separated frontend and backend responsibilities, allowing both teams to work independently and integrate later in the development process.

Built the first phase of the website as a standalone Jekyll implementation, creating the templates, styles, responsive layouts, and interactive components that would later be integrated into Drupal.

Developed interactive experiences including background videos, carousels, accordions, modals, and other reusable UI elements.

Worked through the transition from the standalone frontend implementation to Drupal, adapting the templates and components to work with CMS-managed content.
items.overview:
Redesign of the official Armor All website, developed using a two-phase approach that allowed frontend and backend teams to work independently before integrating the final experience into Drupal.

During the first phase, the complete frontend was built as a standalone Jekyll site, including page templates, responsive layouts, and interactive components. The second phase focused on integrating those templates and functionality into Drupal.

I developed application functionality using Node.js and MongoDB, including job management, candidate applications, and administrative workflows, while also implementing the frontend interfaces and responsive styles.
items.key_points:
Developed a custom recruiting platform that supported both public job applications and internal recruiting workflows.

Built backend functionality using Node.js and MongoDB to manage job positions, candidate information, applications, and administrative operations.

Developed an administration interface that allowed the recruiting team to create and manage job openings and review candidate résumés and portfolios.

Worked across frontend, backend, database, and deployment, providing end-to-end development for the platform.
items.overview:

The platform included a public careers experience where candidates could explore available positions and submit their information, as well as an internal administration area for the recruiting team to manage jobs and review applications.

items.my_role:

I also created a component style guide that documented the different UI elements, allowing the backend team to integrate the frontend into their existing platform without needing to recreate the presentation layer.
items.key_points:
Built the complete presentation layer of the redesigned Café Britt website, transforming the visual designs into responsive and reusable frontend components.

Created a component style guide that documented the website's UI and provided implementation-ready code for the backend team, simplifying the integration between frontend and backend development.

Structured the frontend so that presentation and backend functionality could be developed independently and integrated later.

Used the architecture created for the project as the foundation for Stylekyll, a reusable Jekyll-based starter project that I later published on GitHub.
items.overview:
Redesign of the official Café Britt website, focused on building the complete presentation layer and creating a reusable frontend foundation for integration with the existing backend.

The project separated frontend implementation from backend development, providing the Café Britt team with documented components and ready-to-integrate HTML, styles, and frontend functionality.

items.headline: Criticalmass - The Beginning
items.tech_stack:

- Sass

- Cordova
- REST APIs
- HTML

items.my_role:
As a Developer, I worked across multiple client projects and technologies, developing frontend experiences, email campaigns, CMS integrations, APIs, and mobile applications.

Working with large international clients and multidisciplinary teams also gave me early experience delivering production work under demanding timelines while progressively taking on more technical responsibility.
items.key_points:
Developed digital experiences for internationally recognized brands, working across websites, email campaigns, mobile applications, CMS platforms, and custom APIs.

Built email experiences for major brands such as Adidas and gained strong fundamentals in HTML and CSS by supporting legacy browsers and working through complex cross-browser compatibility challenges.

Contributed to my first mobile application published in an app store using Cordova and gained early experience building applications that separated frontend experiences from backend services.

Expanded from frontend development into technologies such as AngularJS, Node.js, WordPress, APIs, and mobile development while progressively taking on more responsibility within project teams.

Developed early leadership and problem-solving skills while working with multidisciplinary teams, demanding delivery schedules, and large international clients.
items.overview:
Critical Mass was where I started my professional career in web development, working on digital experiences for large international brands and gaining exposure to a wide variety of technologies and development challenges.

During this period, I worked across websites, email development, mobile applications, APIs, CMS integrations, and some of my earliest experiences with decoupled frontend and backend architectures.
